Items.Authors: Eliad Peretz, john C. Mather, Stuart B. Shaklan, Ahmed M. Mohamed, Marc Boucher, Jean T. Landry, Christine E. Gregg
Items.Title: Inflatable starshade architectures for direct imaging of earthlike exoplanets
Items.Abstract: Inflatable starshades offer a path to achieving the large apertures required for direct imaging of Earth-like exoplanets without the mass, volume, and deployment complexity of rigid architectures. We present an inflatable starshade design that integrates petal-based torus geometry, Kapton–resin laminates for post-deployment rigidization, and a simplified inflation system, enabling stowage within standard launch fairings. Recent structural and thermal analyses demonstrate that the inflatable framework can withstand lateral and vertical disturbances with acceptable safety margins, while identifying thermal gradients as the primary driver of dimensional instability. A baseline architecture is used to evaluate edge fidelity, deployment repeatability, mass drivers, and shielding strategies. We discuss requirements, risks, and the path toward sub-millimeter precision needed for 10⁻¹⁰ contrast. This work outlines the feasibility and remaining challenges of inflatable starshade

Items.Authors: Giulia Baroni, Riccardo Campana, Yuri Evangelista, Alejandro Guzmán, Paul Hedderman, Ezequiel Marchesini, Giuseppe Dilillo, Giovanni Della Casa, Francesco Ceraudo, Michele Trenti, Jack McRobbie, Robert Mearns, Matthew Thomas, Miguel Ortiz Del Castillo, Yijie Tao, Simon Barraclough, Airlie Chapman, Simone Pirrotta, Simonetta Puccetti, Matteo Perri, Andrea Santangelo, Tommaso Fagotto, Sara Trevisan, Marco Citossi, Fabrizio Fiore, Wladimiro Leone, Giuseppe Bertuccio, Filippo Mele, Piero Malcovati, Marco Grassi, Evgeny Demenev, Pierluigi Bellutti, Giancarlo Pepponi, Paolo Nogara, Francesco Russo, Giuseppe Sottile, Giovanni La Rosa, Gianluigi Zampa, Nicola Zampa, Tianxiang Chen, Na Gao, Shaolin Xiong, Shoushan Zhang, Shu-Xu Yi
Items.Title: In-flight performance and observations of the high-energy HERMES payload onboard SpIRIT and HERMES-PF
Items.Abstract: The Space Industry Responsive Intelligent Thermal (SpIRIT) mission is a 6U CubeSat developed through collaboration between Australia and Italy for high-energy astrophysics. The 6U CubeSat carries an actively cooled detector system in a Sun-Synchronous orbit. This payload is a compact X-ray and gamma-ray instrument identical to the six units developed by INAF for the Italian Space Agency's HERMES Pathfinder mission. It is designed to detect and locate high-energy transients such as GRBs. SpIRIT was successfully launched on December 1, 2023, aboard a SpaceX Falcon~9, and payload commissioning has been completed. Since October 2025, SpIRIT has been operating in standard Observation mode, with short daily activations and on-board data storage. This paper presents an overview of the orbital operations of the SpIRIT scientific payload, focusing on in-flight calibration activities, scientific observations, and the first-light results of the HERMES-PF mission.

Items.Authors: Benjamin J. S. Pope
Items.Title: Information in interferometric and coronagraphic imaging
Items.Abstract: It is well-known that a diffraction-limited image contains only a finite amount of information about spatial structures in a scene. Using new analytic expressions for the interferometric visibilities of stars, and new calculations of Fisher Information matrices powered by automatic differentiation, we can quantify the degrees of freedom present in interferometric, direct, and coronagraphic images as a function of bandwidth, sampling, positioning, and field of view; and how prior information and complementary observations are best used to break degeneracies.

Items.Authors: Dominic F. Sanchez, B. Gerard, W. Waswa, A. Geringer-Sameth, A. Sengupta, A. Perloff, M. Messerly, W. Moore, M. Cook, P. Pax, C. Laguna, M DeMartino, K. Bundy, R. Jensen-Clem, A. Lemmer, S. M. Ammons, M. Eckart, L. Poyneer, E. Strang
Items.Title: Initial modeling and testbed feasibility studies of WaveDriver: a laser guide star AO system for HWO
Items.Abstract: The Habitable Worlds Observatory will require >100× greater wavefront stability than achieved by JWST, pushing conventional telescope architectures to picometer-level performance limits. WaveDriver is a mission concept that relaxes these constraints by employing an external laser guide star (LGS) spacecraft flying in formation with HWO to enable wavefront sensing and control. Early results from the High Contrast Testbed demonstrate feasibility of required stability using coronagraphs, multiple deformable mirrors, and a suite of wavefront sensors. We report initial stability metrics, sensor performance comparisons, and an optical model quantifying anisoplanatic errors from finite LGS separation.     This work was performed under the auspices of the U.S. Department of Energy by Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory under Contract DE-AC52-07NA27344. This document number is LLNL-ABS-2013921.

Items.Authors: Neil T. Zimmerman, Tyler D. Groff, Guangjun Gao, Michael W. McElwain, Victor J. Chambers, Evan Bray, Enrico Biancalani
Items.Title: Integral field spectroscopy with a Habitable Worlds Observatory coronagraph instrument: design concepts and technology demonstrations
Items.Abstract: In combination with a starlight suppression system, integral field spectroscopy is a promising technique for characterizing directly imaged exoplanets. In typical implementations, the region of interest around an occulted star is spatially sampled with a microlens array and spectrally dispersed in collimated space. The dispersed light is focused onto a detector to record a grid of spectra that can be remapped to a data cube. Here we describe reflective designs that improve the efficiency of the IFS cameras baselined by recent mission concept studies. By applying anamorphic magnification with freeform mirrors, the number of detector pixels per resolution element can be halved, significantly reducing the integration times needed to detect atmospheric absorption features. We also summarize plans to demonstrate the first combined operation of an IFS with a coronagraph in a vacuum testbed at contrast levels below 1E-9 over a 20% spectroscopic bandpass.

Items.Authors: Mo Zhang, Jingwei Hu, Yuan Liu, Chichuan Jin, Weimin Yuan
Items.Title: Integrating Grafana-based visualization and collaborative toolchains to enhance scheduling and science operations in the Einstein Probe mission
Items.Abstract: This poster introduces an integrated engineering toolchain designed to support the EP mission’s scheduling and duty operations. A customized Grafana monitoring layer, built on top of mission databases and real-time data streams, provides engineering visibility into scheduling logic and observation-segment execution. These dashboards enable rapid visualization of the current observation timeline and serve as a useful aid for ToO submissions.    Complementing the monitoring stack, Feishu (Lark) is used as an operational control and notification platform, supporting automated duty alerts and coordinated communication. In addition, YouTrack provides an engineering-grade issue-tracking environment for managing anomaly reports, software defects, service-integration tasks, and long-term operational improvements.

Items.Authors: Keigo Enya, Shingo Kameda
Items.Title: Japan’s possible contributions to the Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO)
Items.Abstract: This paper presents the latest status of Japan’s possible contributions to the Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO). Japan’s wide scientific community, spanning exoplanet science, Solar System science, general astronomy, and astrophysics, has demonstrated strong interest in the HWO mission. The ISAS HWO Study Task Force (ISAS HWO TF) was established within JAXA/ISAS to lead Japanese participation. Regarding hardware contributions, Japan is currently evaluating options for both coronagraph and ultraviolet (UV) instruments, ranging from the instrument level to small components. Leveraging funding from the ISAS Technology Front-Loading Program, technology development is underway for both instruments. One ex-officio member from Japan serves on the Community Science & Instrument Team (CSIT) for the HWO.

Items.Authors: Helen M. McGregor, Max Hewlett, Nick Cerneaz, Sambath Non, Ross Zhelem, Dani Guzman, Qiongjie Lou, Jon Lawrence, Lew Waller, Jae-Woo Kim, Ho Seong Hwang
Items.Title: KSPEC: spectrograph optimization, from TAIPAN to KSPEC
Items.Abstract: The K-SPEC project is led by a consortium of Korean institutes, including Seoul National University (SNU), the Korea Astronomy and Space Science Institute (KASI), and the Korea Institute for Advanced Study (KIAS). The spectrograph will be installed on KMTNet and is a modified version of the TAIPAN spectrograph, which was previously installed and commissioned on the UKST at Siding Spring Observatory. The KPEC spectrograph has been designed and developed by the AAO, building on the optomechanical expertise gained through the development of multiple spectrographs. This paper provides a detailed overview of the opto-mechanical build, emphasizing design choices that enable ease of manufacture, assembly, and alignment. Component fabrication, assembly, testing, and alignment. This paper focuses on the optimization and features build into this 3rd generation spectrograph.

Items.Authors: R. Ligi, S. Lagarde, R. Petrov, S. Robbe-Dubois, J. Dejonghe, F. Allouche, X. Teng, W. Wei, M. Hadjara, A. Boskri
Items.Title: Laboratory characterization of Hierarchical Fringe Tracking
Items.Abstract: One of the main limitations in long-baseline interferometry lies in its fringe tracking sensitivity. The challenge is therefore to maximize this sensitivity while minimizing the spreading of the signal on the detector. This is the goal at the core of the hierarchical fringe tracking (HFT) concept.  We present the laboratory characterization of the 2nd generation HFT chips operating in the near infrared (J and H bands) for up to 6 telescopes with more linear phase and group delay estimators, allowing a strong simplification of the tracking algorithm.   We show direct comparison of the limiting sensitivity of fringe sensing between 6-telescopes HFT and ABCD pairwise chips and demonstrate that the new HFT architecture provides a minimum (#telescopes-1) gain independently of the number of apertures.  Ultimately, this new chip is intended for implementation on the VLTI, CHARA or on the future Xuyi 100m-baseline Stellar Interferometer using three telescopes.

Items.Authors: Clarissa R. Do Ó, Kane Sjoberg, Luke Lamitina, Susan Redmond, Dimitri Mawet, Jorge Llop-Sayson, Siria Alicata
Items.Title: Laboratory demonstration of low order wavefront control using light reflected off the vortex coronagraph
Items.Abstract: The Astro2020 decadal survey identified exoplanet imaging as a priority for the Habitable Worlds Observatory, which will require exo-Earth characterization at 1e-10 contrast. The vortex coronagraph (VC) is a promising candidate for this task due to its small inner working angle and high throughput. We present the first laboratory demonstration of a low-order wavefront sensing and control (LOWFS) tip-tilt loop using light reflected from a VC on Caltech's High Contrast Spectroscopy Testbed (HCST). HCST recently underwent a software upgrade to CATKit2, enabling efficient implementation of phase retrieval, electric field conjugation, and LOWFS control. Over 12 hours, LOWFS tracking shows PSF drift is correlated with bench temperature. Closing the LOWFS tip-tilt loop suppresses drift by >100x, maintains pointing at <0.005 λ/D and preserves a 5e-8 dark hole, while open loop drift degrades contrast by 10x within the same timeframe.

Items.Authors: Salah Oudjertli
Items.Title: Lanthanide-activated graphene for visible-IR interferometry and x-ray-correlated defect imaging
Items.Abstract: Advancing the integration of atomic-scale electronic engineering with high-precision optical diagnostics represents a critical frontier for materials science and intelligent manufacturing. Here, we introduce a lanthanide co-doping strategy in graphene—incorporating neodymium (0.5 at.%) and cerium (0.5–1.0 at.%) to activate optically responsive defect states that broaden graphene’s interaction with light from the visible to the near-infrared. Comprehensive structural and spectroscopic interrogation, combining Raman mapping, XPS, EXAFS, and time-resolved photoluminescence, reveals synergistic 4f–5d transitions that yield stable, wavelength-selective emission profiles spanning 400–1600 nm.  When integrated into wafer-scale architectures, the Nd/Ce co-doped graphene enables a >4-fold enhancement in hyperspectral contrast relative to pristine graphene, significantly boosting the sensitivity of visible–IR interferometric metrology. Items.Authors: Masashi Omiya, Hajime Inaba, Jun Nishikawa, Sho Okubo, Akira Arai, Yuki Moritani, Hideyuki Izumiura, Wako Aoki, Tomonori Usuda, Akito Tajitsu, Eiji Kambe, Bun'ei Sato, Toru Misawa
Items.Title: Laser frequency comb with an integrated fiber-feed system for Subaru/HDS
Items.Abstract: We report on an optical fiber-feed system for injecting an optical laser frequency comb into the High Dispersion Spectrograph (HDS) on the Subaru telescope. The comb, designed for HDS, provides evenly spaced emission lines with a mode spacing of ~30GHz across three wavelength ranges: 350-420 nm, 450-560 nm, 660-900 nm, using an erbium-doped fiber-based femtosecond laser. We developed the fiber-feed module (FFM) to deliver both stellar light and the comb beam to the HDS through the Nasmyth focus via optical fibers. The FFM consists of a fiber input system mounted on the AG/SH flange at the Nasmyth focus, a fiber and scrambling system, and a fiber output system that simultaneously feeds both optical paths to the HDS slit. This calibration system, integrating the comb and the FFM, enables highly precise measurements of stellar radial velocities and will contribute to research on exoplanets and distant galaxies.

Items.Authors: Reagen Leimbach, Shelley Wright, Jerome Maire, Aaron Brown, Bryson Cale, Man Yin Leo Lee, James Wiley, Maren Cosens, Chris Johnson, Renate Kupke, Evan Kress, James Larkin, Kenneth Magnone, Eric Wang, Tucker Jones, Andrew Kramer, Nate Magari, Nicholas McDonald, Kanaka Warad
Items.Title: Liger at W.M. Keck Observatory: imager detector assembly and characterization
Items.Abstract: Liger is a next generation imager and integral field spectroscoper that utilizes a hybrid design to enable simultaneous observations with both setups. In this paper, we present the detector assembly, characterization, and readout processing results of the Liger imager. The focus position and distance of the assembly and the detector, pick-off mirror apparatus will be finely adjusted and tested in both warm and cold environments.

Items.Authors: Jordan D. Wheeler, Jason Austermann, Anna K. Vaskuri, Michael Vissers, Johannes Hubmayr, James Beall, Jeffrey van Lanen, Johnathon Gard, Douglas Bennett, Joel Ullom
Items.Title: Low Tc KIDs for the far infrared
Items.Abstract: Low Tc detector materials for Kinetic Inductance Detectors (KIDs) can enhance sensitivity by reducing the superconducting gap energy and achieving longer quasiparticle lifetimes. In addition, higher normal-state resistivity can enable free-space impedance matching with less detector volume, further increasing detector sensitivity. We explore titanium-based materials, specifically low Tc TiN/Ti multilayer films and Al/Ti multilayer films, to lower Tc and increase resistivity. The potential of these films is evaluated with measurements of optical efficiency and noise-equivalent power (NEP) for far-infrared detector prototypes at 350 μm. The designs aim to enable high-filling-factor pixels without focal plane focusing optics for future far-infrared space applications.

Items.Authors: Brandon Mechtley, Matthieu Bec, Juan Carlos Guerra, Albert Conrad
Items.Title: Low-latency streaming web interfaces at the Large Binocular Telescope Observatory
Items.Abstract: This paper describes the motivation for and implementation of a distributed streaming telemetry pipeline for  web interfaces at the Large Binocular Telescope Observatory, including displays for the SOUL adaptive optics,  telescope metrology, telescope status, and environmental subsystems. Increased demand for remote operation  and more teams operating simultaneously have resulted in higher latency for remote X11 and X2Go sessions,  motivating the development of a distributed web framework for telemetry dashboards and control interfaces. We  have built this framework into our Data Mining System web architecture using Redis for a key-value store and  publish/subscribe messaging, a custom ZeroMQ-to-WebSocket gateway, modular frontend interfaces using the  LitElement web component framework, and real-time charts using Chart.js. Finally, we discuss a searchable log  and telemetry interface implemented at LBTO using the Elasticsearch, Logstash, and Kibana (ELK) stack.

Items.Authors: Songxin Dai, Hangxin Ji, Haoran Yu, Cheng Liao, Lili Wang, Wei Guo, Mingming Xu
Items.Title: Low-resolution Fast Transient spectrograph for 3.8m telescope
Items.Abstract: The Low-resolution Fast Transient Spectrograph is a low-dispersion spectrograph jointly developed by the University of Science and Technology of China(USTC) and the Nanjing Institute of Astronomical Optics & Technology(NIAOT), for the 3.8-meter telescope at the Timau observation station in Indonesia. Its primary scientific objective is to conduct rapid and efficient spectroscopic follow-up observations of transient sources discovered in time-domain surveys. LOFTS covers a broad wavelength range from 370 nm to 1000 nm. When using a 1.3″ slit, the spectral resolution reaches R ≥ 750 at 495 nm and R ≥ 1000 at 750 nm; The peak optical efficiency of the spectrograph is no less than 35%, excluding losses from the slit and detector. This paper presents the detailed optical design of LOFTS and describes its mechanical structure and control system architecture.

Items.Authors: Hari B. Subedi, Scott D. Will, Alan Gostin, Tyler D. Groff
Items.Title: Lyot-based low-order wavefront sensor (LLOWFS) for the Habitable Worlds Observatory
Items.Abstract: The Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) coronagraph contrast stability required to differentiate planets from residual speckles in the dark hole and to detect planets with proper signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) drives very tight tolerances for wavefront variation. The wavefront needs to be stable within 10 pm over 10 minutes and the tip-tilt control needs to be at the sub-milliarcsecond level. Here we describe a Lyot-based low-order wavefront sensor (LLOWFS) for the Exploratory Analytic Case 1 (EAC1) design for the HWO using the scalar vortex coronagraph (SVC) to estimate dynamic low-order wavefront aberrations. The LLOWFS uses rejected starlight from the Lyot stop and slightly defocused images to infer thermally induced low-order aberrations. In this paper, we review the theory of LLOWFS operation, describe the LLOWFS algorithm, and summarize various numerical sensitivity studies on sensor performance.

Items.Authors: Nuno Morujão, Carlos Correia, Felipe Guzmán, Guillaume Bourdarot, Jean-Baptiste Le Bouquin, Denis Defrère, Frank Eisenhauer, Sebastian F. Hönig, Laura Kreidberg, Arseniy Kuznetsov, Romain Laugier, Thibaut Paumard, Esteban Vera Rojas, Paulo Garcia
Items.Title: Machine learning enforced fringe tracking control at the VLTI
Items.Abstract: Mitigating Optical Path Difference (OPD) jitter is critical for the VLTI's GRAVITY+ instrument. Current Kalman filtering yields residuals of 100–150 nm, limiting performance. We propose a Machine Learning (ML) approach to bridge the gap to the fundamental limit.    Using real on-sky telemetry and a calibrated simulator, we trained an LSTM neural network to control the fringe tracking loop. Comparing this with classical methods, we demonstrate that ML performs better in handling non-linear telescope vibrations.    This work lays the foundation for neural Real-Time Control. By targeting the ~30 nm atmospheric residual limit, this approach could allow a 14-fold increase in integration time. Consequently, this software-driven evolution unlocks a sensitivity gain of nearly three magnitudes, significantly expanding the scientific reach of the VLTI.

Items.Authors: Nico Soto, Povilas Palunas
Items.Title: MACO: updating active optics control for the Magellan telescopes
Items.Abstract: We present MACO (Magellan ACtive Optics), an effort to update the wavefront control software for the 6.5m Magellan telescopes. MACO implements modal wavefront control using an orthogonal basis in slope space spanning both primary and secondary mirror degrees of freedom, ensuring well-separated, non-degenerate control modes ordered by required force. The system provides real-time visualization for operation and offline analysis for troubleshooting, supporting both legacy and upgraded guide cameras. Engineering and commissioning results show geometrical residuals of 0.04" RMS with seeing-limited image quality, and actuator forces that settle within half the available range as observations progress.

Items.Authors: Jacob Pember, Ioannis Argyriou, Gerardo Avila, Alexis Brandeker, Lars A. Buchhave, Heather Cegla, David Coutts, Wim De Meester, Joris De Ridder, Denis Defrère, Alistair Glasse, Manuel Güdel, Mariam Haidar, Kaustubh Hakim, Samuel Halverson, Joel Harman, Nicholas Jannsen, Markus Janson, Ailidh Kinney, Suzanne Kovacs, Romain Laugier, Matteo Mallia, Christopher Miller, Kwinten Missiaen, Benjamin Montet, Johan Morren, Enric Pallé, Jesús Pérez Padilla, Wim Pessemier, Don Pollacco, Benjamin Pope, Saskia Prins, Andreas Quirrenbach, Alex Raskin, Gert Raskin, Maddalena Reggiani, Ignasi Ribas, Hugues Sana, Tommy Sandu, Christian Schwab, Dries Seynaeve, Robyn Sharman, Julien Storm, Julian Stürmer, Giovanna Tinetti, Andrew Tkachenko, Hans Van Winckel, Bart Vandenbussche, Pieter Vuylsteke, Chris Waring, Rob Wittenmyer, Duncan Wright, Yanjun Zhou, Nick Binos, Jurek Brzeski, Zhemin Cai, Timothy Chin, Simon Ellis, Tony Farrel, Tobias Feger, Ali Ghari Zadeh, Dani Guzman, Yevgen Kripak, Nirmala Kunwar, Celestina Lacombe, Jon Lawrence, Helen McGregor, David Robertson, Sana Syed, Lew Waller, Jahanzeb Zahoor, Ross Zhelem
Items.Title: MARVEL: approaching instrument assembly and commissioning
Items.Abstract: The MARVEL dedicated radial velocity facility will soon be commissioned at the Mercator Observatory at La Palma, Spain. MARVEL comprises four 0.8m telescopes, each feeding starlight via optical fibres into a single high-resolution spectrograph tuned for precision radial velocity measurements. The four telescopes and their domes have been successfully installed at the observatory site, and are regularly being used for initial photometric observations. In this proceeding we provide a general status update of the facility, covering the procurement, assembly, and laboratory testing of spectrometer optics, mechanics, and detector; developments in the calibration system; the PLC-based control software; the dedicated solar telescope; and a photometry programme that is already underway, making use of the MARVEL telescopes before the installation of the spectrograph.

Items.Authors: Jacob Pember, Gert Raskin, Christian Schwab, Matteo Mallia, Wim Pessemier, Johan Morren, Julien Storm, Pieter Vuylsteke, Andreas Croes, Gerardo Avila, Bart Vandenbussche, Hans Van Winckel
Items.Title: MARVEL: design and implementation of the telescope front-end modules
Items.Abstract: MARVEL is an upcoming dedicated radial velocity facility that will soon be commissioned at the Mercator Observatory at La Palma, Spain. The MARVEL facility comprises four 0.8m telescopes, each feeding via optical fibres a single high-resolution spectrograph specialised for precision radial velocity measurements. Mounted on each MARVEL telescope is a front-end module providing several critical functions, including atmospheric dispersion correction, fast guiding capability, and efficient coupling of starlight—as well as calibration light—into the optical fibres. In this proceeding we present the design and development of these front-end modules and outline our plan for their integration at the observatory.

Items.Authors: Mariam Haidar, Gert Raskin, Christian Schwab, Julian Stuermer, Jacob Pember, Joris De Ridder, David Coutts, Tobias Feger, Daniel Krolikowski, Stanimir O. Letchev, Bart Vandenbussche, Hans Van Winckel
Items.Title: MARVEL: updates to the calibration system and strategy
Items.Abstract: Stable and precise wavelength calibration is absolutely critical in measuring the radial velocity (RV) signatures imparted on stellar hosts by extrasolar planetary companions. The MARVEL (Mercator Array for Radial VELocities) facility will host a cross-dispersed, high-resolution echelle spectrograph, fiber-fed by four 0.8m telescopes, with the resulting spectra recorded on a single detector alongside that of a simultaneous calibration source. This dedicated surveying facility will provide essential ground-based RV follow-up on transit measurements by previous and upcoming space missions. MARVEL aims for an RV measurement precision of 1 m/s, requiring a suite of state-of-the-art calibration tools and techniques capable of developing a wavelength solution stable to the sub-m/s level over long timescales. In this work, we provide an overview of the inner workings of the MARVEL calibration unit and outline updates made to our calibration strategy in anticipation of first light in 2026.

Items.Authors: Arianna Saba, Giorgio Savini, Ian Stotesbury, Harry Johnson, Philip Windred, Richard Archer, Giovanna Tinetti, Marcell Tessenyi, Fabio Favata, Benjamin Wilcock, Sharafina Razin, Parul Janagal, Imogen Garlick
Items.Title: Mauve: the first commercial spectrophotometric UV satellite for astrophysical observations
Items.Abstract: Mauve is a 16U small satellite designed and operated by Blue Skies Space Ltd, built on a C3S platform with a fine guidance system provided by ISISPACE. The payload incorporates commercial off-the-shelf components, including a 13 cm MediaLario telescope (adapted from laser-communication use), a commercially modified fibre from CeramOptec, and a standard configuration NEXOS spectrometer from Avantes. Mauve was launched on 28 November 2025 into a 10:30 LTDN Sun-synchronous low-earth orbit. The mission is designed to perform spectrophotometric measurements of bright stars across the 200–700 nm range to support stellar and exoplanet science. In this paper, we present the Mauve design architecture, commissioning results, and the initial performance of the spacecraft. At the time of submission (six days after launch), the mission remains in the early operations phase. Updates to this abstract may follow as commissioning progresses in the coming weeks and months.

Items.Authors: Dionne Haynes, Andrew Kruse, Antony Galla, Greg Jolley, Israel Vaughn, Trevor Mendel, David Brodrick, Jesse Cranney, Francois Rigaut, Gaston Gausachs, Annino Vaccarella, Hana Benhizia, Tristan Monnier, Roger Haynes, Elia Costa, Bernardo Salasnich, Kalyan Radhakrishnan, Enrico Pinna, Mirko Colapietro, Davide Greggio, Oleksandra Rebrysh, Luca Marafatto, Matteo Aliverti, Pierre Haguenauer, Ulf Seemann
Items.Title: MAVIS: calibration unit final design
Items.Abstract: The MAVIS Calibration Unit (CU) is a dedicated subsystem of the MCAO-Assisted Visible Imager and Spectrograph (MAVIS) instrument for the ESO Very Large Telescope (VLT). Its primary role is to deliver precise calibration for the Imager, Spectrograph, and Adaptive Optics Module, ensuring optimal scientific performance. The CU design incorporates multiple modules—Main Calibration Module (MCM), Light Source Module (LSM), Astrometric Calibration Module (ACM), and Calibration Control Module (CCM)—to support a wide range of calibration functions, including optical distortion correction, non-common-path aberration calibration, spectral calibration, flat-fielding, wavefront sensor alignment, and instrument alignment. The design integrates advanced opto-mechanical assemblies, precision motion stages, and robust control systems to ensure high accuracy and reliability under operational conditions at the VLT. This paper presents the CU final design, detailing the architecture, interfaces, optical a

Items.Authors: Kalyan Kumar Radhakrishnan Santhakumari, Valentina Viotto, Francois Rigaut, Jesse Cranney, Davide Greggio, Luca Marafatto, Guido Agapito, Andrea Baruffolo, Bernardo Salasnich, Elia Costa, Daniela Fantinel, Mirko Colapietro, Maria Bergomi, Enrico Pinna, Pierre Haguenauer, David Brodrick, Richard McDermid, Dionne Haynes, Antony Galla, Andrew Kruse
Items.Title: MAVIS: calibration, estimation, and removal of the non-common path aberrations
Items.Abstract: MAVIS is a multi-conjugate adaptive optics–assisted imager and IFU spectrograph for ESO’s VLT (UT4), operating in the visible. Its adaptive optics module (AOM) provides a uniform 30″ field of view using eight laser guide stars, up to three natural guide stars, and three deformable mirrors. As MAVIS is designed for high-precision astrometry, stringent requirements are imposed on optical quality and residual wavefront error (WFE). Under standard observing conditions, the AOM must deliver an average Strehl ratio ≥8% (goal 12%) for three NGSs with mJ≈8, corresponding to a science-channel WFE of 139 nm (goal 127 nm). This requires calibration and compensation of non-common-path aberrations (NCPAs). MAVIS adopts tomographic phase diversity (TPD), a focal-plane method that estimates aberrations directly from science images and optimises correction using all deformable mirrors. We present the NCPA strategy from laboratory integration to on-sky implementation.

Items.Authors: Gilles Orban de Xivry, Olivier Absil, Iain Hammond, Thomas Bertram, Roy van Boekel, André Boné, Gaël Chauvin, Valentin Christiaens, Dennis Dolkens, Gilles Otten, Prashant Pathak, Nuno Pereira
Items.Title: METIS high-contrast imaging simulations: from instrument modeling to science preparation
Items.Abstract: The High-contrast End-to-End Performance Simulator (HEEPS) has been updated to support the Mid-infrared ELT Imager and Spectrograph (METIS) high-contrast imaging science preparation. Key improvements include final pupil/Lyot stop modeling, as-built NCPA/Talbot effect simulations, and advanced NCPA control strategies using the ALF algorithm. We present comprehensive HCI performance simulations across L-, M-, and N-bands and multiple observing modes, producing updated contrast curves and PSF images. These results demonstrate HEEPS' critical role in bridging METIS instrumentation and scientific readiness for the ELT era.

Items.Authors: Johannes Hubmayr, Jason E. Austermann, Kyuyoung Bae, James E. Beall, Jake E. Connors, Shannon M. Duff, Gregory Jaehnig, Matthew Koc, Michael Link, Tammy Lucas, Christopher Rooney, Corwin Shiu, Joel N. Ullom, Michael R. Vissers
Items.Title: Millimeter-wave component design of OMT-coupled TES detectors
Items.Abstract: Planar Ortho-Mode Transducer coupled transition edge sensor (TES) bolometer arrays fabricated at NIST have been used in instruments such as Advanced ACTPol, SPIDER, and Simons Observatory for measurements of Cosmic Microwave Background polarization. Within each spatial pixel, these devices measure orthogonal polarizations in multiple frequency bands. We present the millimeter-wave design of the on-chip components, which include a coplanar waveguide to microstrip transition, diplexer, stepped impedance low pass filter, microstrip cross-over, 180 degree hybrid, and millimeter-wave power termination located on the TES bolometer island. Focusing on a 90/150 GHz dichroic design, the simulated coupling efficiency of the integrated pixel exceeds 80% in both bands and the cross-polarization is < 0.5%.

Items.Authors: Peter P. Pedersen, Lionel Garcia, Mahshid Alimi, David Degen, Florian Lienhard, Didier Queloz
Items.Title: MIRA: a data management and education platform connecting students to robotic telescopes
Items.Abstract: We present the design of MIRA (Mentored Investigations using Robotic Astronomy), a data management and educational platform that connects Swiss secondary school and undergraduate students with operational robotic observatories.   MIRA structures the entire observation lifecycle: students submit proposals with scientific justifications, instructors moderate and approve proposals via a class view, and approved plans are automatically scheduled against weather and visibility constraints. Following execution, the platform automatically reduces raw FITS frames (including astrometric calibration and photometry) and serves them via a web-accessible archive accompanied by Python-based analysis tutorials.  By separating educational front-ends from low-level telescope controls through Astra and ASCOM Alpaca, MIRA delivers an authentic, scalable, and operationally safe scientific research workflow that bridges classroom learning with professional observatory operations.

Items.Authors: Michael Esselborn, H. Bonnet, C. Diaz Cano, B. Engler, A. Kellerer, J. Kolmeder, O. Pfuhl, A. Rubin, C. Vérinaud, J. Woillez
Items.Title: Mitigating pupil distortion for robust ELT phasing with SHAPS
Items.Abstract: The Shack-Hartmann Phasing Sensor (SHAPS) is the baseline instrument for cophasing the segmented 39-m primary mirror of the Extremely Large Telescope (ELT). Located in the Phasing and Diagnostics Station (PDS), SHAPS employs a modified Shack-Hartmann design to re-image the full 798-segment primary onto a high-precision lenslet array. Meeting the requirement of < 12 mm mapping accuracy in the M1 space is critical for achieving the phase tolerances needed for diffraction-limited performance. Given the tight registration and distortion tolerances, distortion effects pose a significant risk to the SHAPS phasing concept.  We present a risk-mitigation strategy that combines in-field measurement of the as-built pupil distortion during the WFC commissioning phase with the fabrication of a new lenslet array in which the average distortion is deliberately imprinted. The strategy has been successfully validated on the Miniscule ELT (MELT) test bench, demonstrating its feasibility for ELT phasing.

Items.Authors: Julien Drevon, Claudia Paladini, Peter L. Scicluna, Isabelle Percheron, Akke Corporaal
Items.Title: Modeling the VLTI/PIONIER transfer function using machine learning
Items.Abstract: We developed a machine learning framework to model the interferometric Transfer Function (TF) of the VLTI/PIONIER instrument using environmental and instrumental parameters such as seeing, coherence time (τ₀), pressure, temperature, baseline, and wavelength. The goal was to predict and monitor TF variations in real time to improve calibration accuracy. After testing several models, we adopted eXtreme Gradient Boosting, which worked efficiently on both small and large datasets while providing stable and interpretable results. Using over 45,000 visibility measurements collected between 2022 and 2024, the model achieved an R² of about 0.98 on both training and test sets, showing strong predictive performance and generalization. Feature analysis with Variation Inflation Factor and SHapley Additive exPlanations showed that baseline, wavelength, and pressure were the most influential parameters. These findings show that machine learning can provide a reliable solution for TF predictions.

Items.Authors: I. Montilla, L. Montoya, D. Gómez, M. Reyes García-Talavera, P. Wizinowich, M. Troy, J. Castro, H. de Paz, S. Fernández, M. Huertas, G. Lombardi, I. Alvarez, J. Miret
Items.Title: Modelling atmospheric dispersion effects on fine phasing of large segmented mirrors
Items.Abstract: The Gran Telescopio Canarias (GTC), with its segmented primary mirror, needs precise fine phasing for optimal performance. Atmospheric dispersion, which separates light into wavelengths due to atmospheric refraction, can disrupt segment alignment, especially in optical bands when using broadband algorithms. This study investigates the impact of dispersion on cophasing and proposes an atmospheric dispersion model to improve the process. The model estimates distortions caused by dispersion during cophasing, allowing separate measurement of segment piston and dispersion effects, reducing errors. Preliminary results show that correcting for atmospheric dispersion enhances image quality and segment alignment. The model offers a valuable tool for improving segmented mirror telescopes and can be applied to other large-scale observatories.

Items.Authors: Anthony Meilland, Philippe Priolet, Jean-Charles Augereau, Steve Ertel, Thomas Stuber, Jeremy B. Scott, Romain Laugier, Denis Defère
Items.Title: Modelling NOTT nulling-interferometric data using oimodeler and GRaTer
Items.Abstract: We present preparatory work for modeling future data from the VLTI/NOTT instrument, to be installed at Paranal next year as part of the ASGARD suite. Unlike conventional interferometers, NOTT will operate in nulling mode, cancelling stellar light to achieve high contrast and reveal faint nearby material such as exoplanets or circumstellar dust. Because nulling interferometry produces multiple flux measurements depending on the nulling pattern rather than standard observables, its data cannot be stored in OIFITS2 and efforts are underway to define a dedicated NIFITS format. oimodeler, a modular Python package for optical-interferometry modeling fully compatible with OIFITS, has been extended to simulate NIFITS data for NOTT. Our simulations focuses on two main science cases: detecting and characterizing faint binaries and exoplanets, and modeling exozodiacal dust. For the latter, we integrated pyGRaTer an updated python version of the GRaTer radiative-transfer code into oimodeler.

Items.Authors: G. Pascual-Cisneros, S. Della Torre, A. Besnard, F. J. Casas, M. Gervasi, B. Maffei, T. Matsumura, V. Sauvage, F. Piacentini, S. Stever, G. Signorelli, A. Tartari, M. Zannoni
Items.Title: Modelling of the thermal systematics produced by cosmic rays in a sub-K bolometric array in L2
Items.Abstract: The next generation of cosmic microwave background (CMB) instruments aim to reach unprecedented sensitivities, making the characterization and mitigation of instrumental systematic effects increasingly critical. One key effect for space-based CMB missions is the impact of Cosmic Rays (CRs).  In this context, we present a simulation pipeline to simulate time ordered energy deposition data produced by hits of different CR particles on a given focal plane configuration. This data is then used to model thermal fluctuations on the wafer with a custom two-dimensional heat equation solver optimized for this problem, that has been validated against COMSOL Multiphysics simulations.   This pipeline is applied to LiteBIRD satellite configuration finding that thermal fluctuations produced by CR hits can be understood as an additional white-noise contribution comparable to current instrumental requirements, underscoring the need for CR-mitigation techniques.

Items.Authors: Juan M. Altamirano, David Buscher, James Luis, Bodie Seneta
Items.Title: Modernizing the MROI delay line metrology system: a low-latency fiber-optic link
Items.Abstract: This paper presents modernization of the MROI delay line metrology system addressing VME platform obsolescence while enhancing performance. The fiber-optic digital architecture replaces the 200-meter analog link, achieving sub-5 microsecond latency and 10-20 kHz sampling (2-4× improvement) while eliminating electromagnetic vulnerability from lightning strikes. Custom digital signal processing electronics replace obsolete VME hardware, improving low-light sensitivity critical for tracking very dim stars and faint astronomical objects. Working prototypes enable laboratory testing and spare delay line integration. Expected improvements include faster position correction during slewing operations, enhanced disturbance rejection via increased servo bandwidth, and improved optical path difference stability for fringe tracking. This offers a practical modernization pathway extending operational lifetime while significantly enhancing interferometric observation capabilities.

Items.Authors: Manal Chebbo, Laurent Jocou, Patrick Rabou, David Mouillet, Louis Barbier, Lorenzo Busoni, Simonetta Chinellato, Paolo Ciliegi, Jean-Jacques Correia, Andrea Di Rocco, Jacopo Farinato, Italo Foppiani, Sylvain Guieu, Yves Magnard, Demetrio Magrin, Thibaut Moulin, Fabrice Pancher, Edgard Renault, Marco Riva, Sylvain Rochat, Sébastien Soler, Ludovico Teodori
Items.Title: MORFEO @ ELT: laser guide stars wave front sensors module
Items.Abstract: MORFEO (Multi-conjugate adaptive Optics Relay For ELT Observations) is the post-focal adaptive optics module for the ESO Extremely Large Telescope. The instrument provides MCAO correction for two instruments: MICADO and HARMONI.  We present a completed and consistent design for the MORFEO LGSWFS Module, which consists mainly of 6 Shack-Hartmann wavefront sensors mounted on a high-precise rotating and translating platform designed to track the ELT elevation axis. This design satisfies demanding specifications required to achieve high-accuracy wavefront sensing on the ELT.   A key element of each sensor is its micro-lens array (MLA), based on an innovative symmetric double-sided design that ensures telecentricity of the exit beam.   This paper presents the architecture and expected performance of the MORFEO LGSWFS Module, focusing on the rotator, focusing stage, and MLA technologies that enable high-accuracy wavefront sensing on the ELT.

Items.Authors: Edoardo Maria Alberto Redaelli, Marco Riva, Jacopo Farinato, Matteo Tintori, Daniele Galieni, Luca Marafatto, Andrea di Rocco, paolo ciliegi, ludovico teodori
Items.Title: MORFEO @ ELT: Mechanical alignment system for MORFEO optomechanics
Items.Abstract: The MORFEO’s optomechanics are going toward the FDR the interfaces are defined and the alignment system is tested in our lab to prove the designed alignment range and the repeatability of the system. The methodology followed for the characterization of the mechanics is made of three different parts. The first one is the characterization of the kinematics connection, the second on the measure of the single alignment system based on wedge solution. The third step is the metrology of the whole system. In this proceeding it will e reported the final results of the measurement campaign pointing out the different solution used and final design.

Items.Authors: Daphne Diretto, Andrea Baruffolo, Mirko Colapietro, Elia Costa, Benedetta Di Francesco, Fulvio Laudisio, Fabrice Pancher, Bernardo Salasnich
Items.Title: MORFEO@ELT: latest update in the instrument control system software design
Items.Abstract: MORFEO (Multi-conjugate adaptive Optics Relay For ELT Observations) is the post-focal adaptive optics module for the ESO Extremely Large Telescope. It provides MCAO correction for two instruments: MICADO and HARMONI. Thanks to the progress toward the Final Design Review, we present the latest updates to the design of the MORFEO Instrument Control System Software (ICSS). We examine the design approaches and the current work dedicated to guarantee high robustness, modularity, and seamless integration with the ELT software framework. Particular focus will be given to its integration with the MICADO ICSS. We then introduce SAPO (Software for AIT Phase Operation), a dedicated instrument with its control software designed to support the MORFEO assembly, integration and testing phase.

Items.Authors: Marc Baril, Greg Green, William Mahoney, Conrad Holmberg, Cam Wipper
Items.Title: Nānā ao: an all-sky, weather-ready LWIR and visible imager for Maunakea
Items.Abstract: A full view of the night sky is invaluable for observers as they seek to efficiently execute their observations while avoiding cloudy, non-photometric conditions. Imaging in the LWIR band, 8 – 14 µm, allows for the detection of thin cloud cover, whereas visible band imaging can indicate the arrival of thick cloud banks. Maunakea’s all-sky LWIR/VIS imager was recently redesigned to provide a more weather-robust enclosure and support newer sensors. This instrument, Nānā ao, replaces the ASIVA instrument that had been in service since 2011. In addition to the mechanical improvements made, this project represents a first instance of instrumentation development at the Canada France Hawaii Telescope using Gitlab’s continuous-integration/continuous-deployment (CICD) model.

Items.Authors: Nithyanandan Thyagarajan, Bojan Nikolic, Chris Carilli, Laura Torino, Ubaldo Iriso
Items.Title: New techniques for high-resolution imaging and high-precision wavefront sensing via masked-aperture interferometry
Items.Abstract: We present novel techniques for high-precision wavefront sensing and high-resolution imaging using masked-aperture interferometry. Inspired by radio interferometry, these approaches can measure both the amplitude and phase of wavefront distortions while simultaneously reconstructing the source structure. We have demonstrated them on the ALBA synchrotron beamline. The first uses non-redundant aperture masks with a self-calibration algorithm to recover nanometer-scale pathlength errors and subarcsecond-scale source structure. The second employs closure invariants from these masks bypassing self-calibration while retaining comparable fidelity. The third extends self-calibration to redundant masks, enabling higher photon throughput without compromising reconstruction performance. These methods form a robust framework for high-resolution interferometry in photon-limited cases with applications from accelerator diagnostics to astronomical facilities like the James Webb Space Telescope.

Items.Authors: Grecia Falcon, Imraan Bokhari, Eric Grigel
Items.Title: ngVLA 18m antenna preliminary foundation study
Items.Abstract: The ngVLA main antenna array is comprised of 244 antennas, with its core located at the VLA site in New Mexico and extending across multiple states, including sites in Mexico. While the core location is well established, the remaining antenna sites are still under evaluation. To assess the influence of soil variability on the 18-m antenna foundation, a study was conducted to identify an optimal preliminary foundation design that could be implemented across different site conditions with minimal modification. This paper presents an overview of the study and provides insight into how variations in soil properties affect the rotational stiffness of the foundation and, ultimately, the antenna pointing error. The findings from this work support the project’s planning efforts by guiding site selection, foundation design standardization, and overall construction cost optimization.

Items.Authors: Timothy M. C. Abbott, Jesse Ball, Eric J. Christensen, Heidi Schweiker, Ariel Lopez, John P. Blakeslee
Items.Title: Night-time operations under NOIRLab
Items.Abstract: As part of the introduction of matrix management, NOIRLab's night-time telescope operations and observing staff have been combined into the Telescope Operations group. These are the front line personnel at any observatory. They work under unusual pressures, and are uniquely key to the success of the astronomical exercise. We have integrated several long-established, distinct, and individually effective philosophies, plus Rubin's new approach, into an overarching structure which enables evolution into greater unity, mutual support, and responsiveness to NOIRLab's needs, without degrading each site's ability to operate their own facility with their customary maximum efficiency. In this paper, we discuss the roles of the night staff at NOIRLab's diverse observatories, how they meet the various demands at each facility, the challenges of managing these critical workers across multiple sites and professional cultures, and the lessons we have learned doing so over the past 5 years.

Items.Authors: J. Redford, P. S. Barry, M. Becerril-Tapia, C. Benson, C. M. Bradford, T. Brien, S. Doyle, V. Gómez-Rivera, S. Hailey-Dunsheath, J. Hernández-Aguilar, J. L. Hernández-Rebollar, D. Hughes, E. Kane, K. S. Karkare, A. Lapuente, R. McGeehan, R. Naranjo-Romero, A. Papageorgiou, I. Rodríguez-Montoya, S. Rowe, D. Sánchez-Arguelles, S. Savorgnano, A. Tan, J. Vega-Méndez
Items.Title: Noise and sensitivity analysis of SuMaC on-sky and in lab
Items.Abstract: We present the on sky sensitivity of the SuperSpec-MUSCAT Collaboration (SuMAC). SuperSpec is a microwave kinetic inductance detector (MKID) based on-chip spectrometer with an R ~ 200 covering 200 - 300 GHz band. In July of 2025, SuperSpec devices were installed into the MUSCAT instrument and observed on-sky at the Large Millimeter Telescope (LMT) in July and August.  The spectral characterization and performance of the individual channels will be discussed, both in lab testing and the performance on-sky in the SuMAC setup, along with the extrapolated sensitivities of optimal conditions at the LMT.

Items.Authors: Glenn P. Brossus, Marianne Cox, Richard Demers, Barbara Fischer, Frank Groark, William Burgett, Arielle Bertrou-Cantou, Juan Pablo Haddad, Bo Xin, Peter Thompson, Hugo Chiquito, Tomas Krasuski, Dave Ashby, Trupti Ranka, Dave Zeller, Fernando Quiros-Pacheco, Jordi Molgo, Josema Filgueira
Items.Title: NSF sponsored risk reduction for the Giant Magellan Telescope (GMT)
Items.Abstract: The NSF has supported risk reduction and prototyping efforts for the US Extremely Large Telescope program, that includes both the Giant Magellan Telescope and the Thirty Meter Telescope. The NSF Sponsored awards, and their impact on the Giant Magellan Telescope are presented herein. Three Awards received over the last 6 years have built and tested hardware that reduce risk, validate designs and verify performance of subsystems required for GMT active and adaptive optics control and performance. The NSF-Development subaward received from AURA built a primary mirror mounting cell and mirror support hardware, the long lead optics and main structural components for the first off-axis adaptive secondary mirror, and two wavefront sensing and control (WFSC) testbeds. Two subsequent awards utilized NSF built hardware to demonstrate active optics performance. Additional work included prototyping Real-Time Computing (RTC) platforms, and the Observatory Control System End-2-End Prototype.

Items.Authors: Julien Storm, Gert Raskin, Bart Vandenbussche, Christian Schwab, Jake Pember, Hugues Sana, Dirk Vandepitte, Leonardo Peri, Sibo Van Gool, Louis Storm, Pierre Royer, Maddalena Reggiani, Camille Pirat, Dominic Bowman
Items.Title: Onboard wavelength calibration of the CubeSpec spectrograph using a Fiber Fabry–Pérot Etalon
Items.Abstract: CubeSpec is a 12U CubeSat mission designed to demonstrate high resolution spectroscopy from a compact platform, with launch readiness targeted for early 2027. Its cross dispersed echelle spectrograph requires an onboard calibration system that is very compact, mechanically robust, and sufficiently stable and precise to meet the mission’s spectral performance requirements. A fiber-based Fabry–Pérot (FFP) etalon provides an attractive solution due to its very small footprint and stable line spacing, though it demands careful thermal stabilization. CubeSpec employs a fiber-coupled LED continuum source to both illuminate the FFP etalon for wavelength calibration and to supply broadband light for order identification and flat-fielding. The light is injected into the spectrograph via optics mounted on the telescope’s secondary mirror. We describe here the design of the FFP calibration unit and its expected performance.

Items.Authors: Shumei Jia, Liming Song, Chengkui Li, Haisheng Zhao, Juan Zhang, Ju Guan, Ge Ou, Jin Wang
Items.Title: Operations of the EP-FXT science data center
Items.Abstract: The Einstein Probe (EP) carries two primary scientific payloads: the Wide-field X-ray Telescope (WXT) and the Follow-up X-ray Telescope (FXT). The EP-FXT Science Data Center (SDC), hosted at the Institute of High Energy Physics (IHEP), is responsible for the production, processing, and management of FXT data. Since the EP’s launch on January 9, 2024, the FXT SDC has maintained smooth operations, encompassing the production and publication of standard data products, the development and release of data analysis software and calibration databases, and the provision of support to scientific users. This paper provides an overview of the center's workflows, core tasks, and operational status.

Items.Authors: Eliad Peretz, Bert Pasquale, Guangjun Gao, Greg Aldering, Saul Prlmutter, Jerry Edelstein, Tim Miller
Items.Title: Optical and mechanical development of the ORKID-II multi-field integral field spectrograph using monolithic machined image slicers
Items.Abstract: ORKID-II is a next-generation integral field spectrograph designed for high-resolution, multi-field imaging and spectroscopy on large ground-based telescopes and future space missions. Building on the ORCAS/ORKID program, the instrument uses monolithic machined image slicers manufactured with sub-micron precision to enable fine, coarse, and very coarse spatial sampling within a compact optical platform. We present the optical and mechanical development of the tri-field IFU, including telecentric, anamorphic, and magnification-optimized designs; Canon-fabricated slicer geometries; system-level packaging; and integration with the telescope relay and spectrograph. ORKID-II demonstrates a scalable approach to wide-field, high-throughput spectroscopy and provides a technology path for future flagship observatories.

Items.Authors: Runa Briguglio, Nicolò Azzaroli, Pietro Ferraiuolo, Marco Xompero, Giorgio Pariani, Luca Oggioni, Riccardo Grignaffini, Armando Riccardi
Items.Title: Optical calibration of ELT-M4: segment phasing procedure tested on the prototype
Items.Abstract: A critical calibration in segmented optical system is the phasing, i.e. the accurate positioning of the segments, in both rotation and piston, in order to approximate a continuous surface. In deformable mirrors, the phasing is part of the flattening procedure and is obtained by the actuators; as a consequence, both high order shapes and rigid body motions shall be controlled accurately.  In this paper we describe the phasing procedure optimized for the ELT adaptive mirror M4 on its Optical Test Tower, and verified on the M4 Demonstration Prototype. The procedure includes the high orders flattening, based on the actuators correction with the feedback of a dynamic interferometer; the interferometer phase ambiguity is solved with an absolute phase sensor measuring a spot across two adjacent segments. Given the peculiarity of the test system, the procedure integrate the reading of both optical sensors with the internal metrology of the M4.

Items.Authors: Riccardo Grignaffini, Luca Oggioni, Runa Briguglio, Giorgio Pariani, Pietro Ferraiuolo, Marco Xompero, Nicolò Azzaroli, Matteo Menessini
Items.Title: Optical calibration of the ELT-M4: validation of the local calibration of capacitive position sensors on the demonstration prototype
Items.Abstract: Adaptive optics is becoming essential for modern telescopes, driving larger and more complex adaptive mirrors such as ELT's M4, whose full performance requires a new flexible and efficient calibration.    In previous work, we proposed an optical calibration method for adaptive mirrors and validated it in a controlled laboratory setup. Its application to the M4 Demonstration Prototype, however, revealed stronger and faster environmental disturbances, which can prevent the reconstruction in time of the phase-ambiguous interferometric measurements.    Here, we further develop the proposed procedure and investigate several strategies to recover a reliable reconstruction under these conditions. In particular, we show that using a stationary shell as an in-frame reference reduces common-mode disturbances and enables robust calibration. The resulting calibration coefficients are physically consistent, validating the procedure for future application to the final ELT-M4 mirror.

Items.Authors: Marcela Izquierdo Poza, Kirit Karkare, John M. Kovac, Colin A. Bischoff, Peter Ade, Zeeshan Ahmed, Mandana Amiri, Denis Barkats, Ritoban Basu Thakur, Dominic Beck, James J. Kang, Kekoa Lasko, Kenny Lau, Margaret R. Lautzenhiser, Scott Mackey, Nolan Maher, Yuka Nakato, Hien T. Nguyen, Roger O'Brient, Anika Patel, Matthew A. Petroff, Annie R. Polish, Clement Pryke, Carl D. Reintsema, Thibault Romand, Maria Salatino, Benjamin L. Schmitt, Baibhav Singari, Aaron Steiger, Bryan Steinbach, Rashmikant Sudiwala, Keith L . Thompson, Clara Vergès, Abigail Vieregg, Albert Wandui, W.L. Kimmy Wu, Cyndia Yu, Lingzhen Zeng, Silvia Zhang
Items.Title: Optical characterization of the BICEP array 150 and 220/270 GHz CMB polarimeters
Items.Abstract: BICEP Array (BA) measures faint polarization in the cosmic microwave background to test cosmic inflation. Each detector’s angular response needs to be precisely measured since beam mismatch between orthogonally polarized detector pairs can leak temperature into polarization and bias the tensor-to-scalar ratio r.   We present new far-field beam measurements for the 2026 season, focusing on characterizing new detectors at 220/270 GHz in the BA3 receiver and consistency checks at 150 GHz in BA2. We also introduce low-level improvements to the beam mapping analysis pipeline leading to better-quantified noise and higher-fidelity beam shapes. These updates yield more reliable characterization of BA beams and help ensure that our control of beam systematics improves commensurately with our sensitivity and limits on inflation.

Items.Authors: John J. Piotrowski, Danielle Frostig, Mark Mueller, David Cruz, Matthew Werneken, Julian Garcia, Daniel Fabricant, Ashley Villar, Ana Bonaca, Phillip A. Cargile, Vedant Chandra, Charles Conroy, Benjamin D. Johnson
Items.Title: Optical design of Boombox: a high-throughput optical spectrograph on dual-hemisphere 6.5-meter telescopes
Items.Abstract: Boombox is a moderate-dispersion optical spectrograph currently being built for the 6.5-meter MMT and Magellan Clay telescope. Boombox, in synergy with the LSST, will provide rapid follow-up spectroscopy of LSST targets to classify the diverse array of expected transient astronomical phenomena and their host galaxies. In this paper, we present the optical design of Boombox and provide a detailed tolerance analysis to ensure manufacturability. Boombox achieves its scientific goals with a two-channel spectrograph covering 3550 to 10100 Å at R ~ 1000. The spectrograph uses 36 dedicated optical fibers (1.2" core diameter) from the Via fiber positioning system distributed across a 1-degree field of view. Boombox leverages binary transmission gratings and a high QE deep-depleted CCD261-04 to achieve high throughput. Finally, we discuss the optical design challenges associated with minimizing spectral crosstalk and provide lessons learned for future spectrograph designs.
